The following is a list of events from the year '''2022 in the United States'''.

Politically, the United States continued to be dominated by a [[culture war]], with the [[Abortion in the United States|issue of abortion]] gaining special attention amidst the Supreme Court's decision to overturn ''[[Roe v. Wade]]'' with its ruling on ''[[Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization]],'' sparking [[2022 abortion protests|protests across the country.]] America also saw labor unions gain increased traction, with [[Apple worker organizations|Apple]], [[Starbucks unions|Starbucks]] and [[Amazon worker organization|Amazon]] among the most notable targets. In conjunction, increased attention to [[critical race theory]], the instruction of [[gender identity]] in schools, and the ongoing investigations into both former president [[Donald Trump]] and the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6th attack]] gained political attention. [[Mass shootings in the United States|Mass shootings]] also became an increasingly common phenomenon, with 641 occurring in 2022 as of December 28, varying from those targeting schools (including [[Robb Elementary School shooting|the deadliest shooting of the year]]) to bias-motivated incidents which have targeted racial and sexual minorities.<ref>{{Cite news |title=US Hate Crimes Rise During First Half of 2022 |work=[[Voice of America]] |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/us-hate-crimes-rise-during-first-half-of-2022-/6713791.html |access-date=November 30, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mass Shootings in 2022 {{!}} Gun Violence Archive |url=https://www.gunviolencearchive.org/reports/mass-shooting |access-date=2022-09-21 |website=www.gunviolencearchive.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Diaz |first=Jaclyn |date=2022-05-25 |title=27 school shootings have taken place so far this year |language=en |work=NPR |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/05/24/1101050970/2022-school-shootings-so-far |access-date=2022-09-21}}</ref>

In the economy, the United States remained heavily impacted by the global [[2021–2022 inflation surge|inflation surge]], a simultaneous [[2022 stock market decline|stock market decline]] and a heavy increase in [[Gas Prices|gasoline prices]], all partly due to [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russia's invasion of Ukraine]]. [[Big Tech|America's largest tech companies]] were hit especially hard by the economy, with [[Meta Platforms]] in particular losing nearly $700 billion in valuation. The [[Federal Reserve]] gained increased attention with a series of its first aggressive interest rate hikes in years, a trend which continued in [[2023 in the United States|2023]], with the [[federal funds rate]] by year's end reaching 4.4%.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web |title=Implementation Note issued December 14, 2022 |url=https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20221214a1.htm |access-date=2022-12-15 |website=Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System |language=en}}</ref> 2022 also marked a period of acquisitions within the tech industry as well, notably [[Elon Musk]]'s [[Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk|acquisition]] of [[Twitter, Inc.|Twitter]] and [[Microsoft]]'s [[Acquisition of Activision Blizzard by Microsoft|ongoing buyout]] of [[Activision Blizzard]]. Later in the year, the US saw the first major challenges to its [[gratuity]] culture; [[tipflation]], as it has since become known, has caused Americans to lower their tips.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dickler |first=Jessica |title=Amid persistent inflation, cash-strapped consumers are tipping less |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/11/25/amid-persistent-inflation-cash-strapped-consumers-are-tipping-less.html |access-date=2023-04-01 |website=CNBC |date=November 25, 2022 |language=en}}</ref>{{horizontal TOC|nonum=yes|align=center}}

== Elections ==
{{Further|2022 United States elections}}

=== Midterm elections ===
The [[2022 United States elections|midterm elections]] were held on November 8, and all 435 voting seats of the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]], 35 seats in the [[United States Senate|Senate]], 39 state and territorial gubernatorial elections, and numerous state and local elections were decided. [[2022 United States Senate election in Georgia|Georgia's Senate election]] went to a runoff between Democrat incumbent [[Raphael Warnock]] and Republican challenger [[Herschel Walker]] a month later, which Warnock ultimately won.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Democratic Sen. Warnock defeats Republican Walker in Georgia runoff |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/georgia-senate-runoff-election-polls-close-results-rcna60156 |access-date=2022-12-07 |website=NBC News |date=December 7, 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

* The Democratic Party maintained their lead in the [[United States Senate|Senate]], retaining all seats previously held and [[2022 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania|picking up a Senate seat from Pennsylvania]]. Senators [[Chuck Schumer]] and [[Mitch McConnell]] are re-elected as Democratic and Republican leaders.<ref>[https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/biden-democrats-celebrate-retaining-control-senate-rcna56956 Biden, Democrats celebrate keeping control of the Senate] NBC News, November 13, 2022</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-15 |title=Senate won for Democrats, 'It's the year of Chuck Schumer' |url=https://apnews.com/article/congress-senate-control-schumer-f4ec767f528843858c42b2c90945dda6 |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=AP NEWS |language=en}}</ref> With [[Patrick Leahy]]'s retirement, [[Patty Murray]] is elected as the next [[President pro tempore of the United States Senate|president pro tempore of the Senate]].<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |date=2022-11-16 |title=Patty Murray likely to be first female Senate president pro tem, 3rd in line for presidency |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/politics/patty-murray-to-be-first-female-senate-president-pro-tempore-third-in-line-for-presidency/ |access-date=2022-12-07 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref>
* The Republican Party retook the House of Representatives. GOP representatives, after an unprecedented 15 rounds of voting, elected Representative [[Kevin McCarthy]] of [[California's 20th congressional district|California's 20th district]] to succeed [[Nancy Pelosi]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Republicans win majority of seats in U.S. House, CBS News projects |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/elections-2022-house-of-representatives-results-control-democrats-republicans/ |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=CBS News |date=November 17, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brooks |first=Emily |date=2022-11-15 |title=McCarthy wins GOP vote for Speakership handily over right-wing challenge |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/house/3736521-mccarthy-wins-gop-vote-for-speakership-handily-over-right-wing-challenge/ |access-date=2022-11-18 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}</ref>
*Democrats [[Katie Hobbs]], [[Wes Moore]] and [[Maura Healey]] flip the governors seats in [[2022 Arizona gubernatorial election|Arizona]], [[2022 Maryland gubernatorial election|Maryland]], and [[2022 Massachusetts gubernatorial election|Massachusetts]] respectively.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2022/11/08/1134199246/massachusetts-governor-results-maura-healey|title=Maura Healey claims historic victory, elected first woman governor in Massachusetts|first=Anthony|last=Brooks|date=November 8, 2022|website=NPR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-11-14 |title=Trump ally Kari Lake loses to Democrat Katie Hobbs in Arizona governor race |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-63627007 |access-date=2022-11-15}}</ref>
*Republican [[Joe Lombardo]] flips the governor's seat in [[2022 Nevada gubernatorial election|Nevada]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Governor Election Results 2022 {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2022/results/governor |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref>

==== Electoral milestones ====

* [[Sarah Huckabee Sanders]] in Arkansas, Maura Healey in Massachusetts, and [[Kathy Hochul]] in New York became the first elected female governors in their states, and [[Katie Britt]] is Alabama's first elected female senator. Healey also became the first [[lesbian]] governor in US history.<ref name="auto1"/>
* [[Alex Padilla]] became California's first elected Latino senator, and [[Delia Ramirez]] is elected as Illinois' first Latina congresswoman.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Mehta |first1=Seema |last2=Fry |first2=Hannah |last3=Castleman |first3=Terry |date=2022-11-09 |title=Alex Padilla makes history as first Latino elected to U.S. Senate from California |url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2022-11-08/2022-california-midterm-election-padilla-first-latino-u-s-senate-california |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bloom |first=Mina |date=2022-11-09 |title=Delia Ramirez Makes History As First Midwestern Latina Headed To Congress |url=https://blockclubchicago.org/2022/11/08/delia-ramirez-makes-history-as-first-midwestern-latina-headed-to-congress/ |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=Block Club Chicago |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Summer Lee]] became Pennsylvania's first Black female representative in the House, and Wes Moore became Maryland's first Black governor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How Summer Lee's historic win in Pa.'s 12th Congressional District reverberates beyond politics |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/news/election2022/2022/11/13/summer-lee-pennsylvania-12th-congressional-district/stories/202211120074 |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-09 |title=Democrat Wes Moore elected governor in historic Maryland race |url=https://www.kosu.org/history/news/2022-11-08/democrat-wes-moore-elected-governor-in-historic-maryland-race |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=KOSU |language=en}}</ref>
*[[Maxwell Frost]], at the age of 25, became the first member of [[Generation Z]] to be elected to Congress.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2022/11/10/1135856130/maxwell-frost-on-becoming-the-first-member-of-gen-z-to-be-elected-to-congress|title=Maxwell Frost on becoming the first member of Gen Z to be elected to Congress|date=10 November 2022|access-date=13 November 2022|website=NPR}}</ref>
*[[Karen Bass]] became the first female [[mayor of Los Angeles]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hubler |first=Shawn |date=2022-11-16 |title=Karen Bass Becomes First Woman Elected as Los Angeles Mayor |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/11/16/us/politics/la-mayor-race-california-caruso-bass.html |access-date=2022-11-17 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

=== Special elections and recalls ===

* [[2022 Florida's 20th congressional district special election|A special election]] was held in [[Florida]] on January 11 to fill a vacancy in its [[Florida's 20th congressional district|20th congressional district]] due to the death of [[Alcee Hastings]] on April 6, 2021. Democrat [[Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick]] wins the election with over 78% of the vote over Republican Jason Mariner.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Coote |first=Darryl |date=January 11, 2022 |title=Democrat Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick wins Florida's District 20 Congressional seat |work=[[United Press International]] |url=https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2022/01/11/Sheila-Cherfilus-McCormick-wins-Florida-election/8321641952206/ |access-date=January 12, 2022}}</ref>
* [[2022 California's 22nd congressional district special election|A special election]] was held in [[California]] to fill a vacancy in its [[California's 22nd congressional district|22nd congressional district]] on June 7 due to the resignation of [[Devin Nunes]] on January 1. Republican [[Connie Conway]] wins the election with over 50% of the vote over Democrat Lourin Hubbard.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brassil |first=Gillian |date=January 9, 2022 |title=These 5 candidates want a shot at Devin Nunes' seat, even if it lasts only 6 months |url=https://www.fresnobee.com/news/politics-government/article257147057.html |access-date=January 9, 2022 |website=fresnobee.com |publisher=[[The Fresno Bee]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
* [[2022 San Francisco District Attorney recall election]]: [[San Francisco District Attorney's Office|San Francisco District Attorney]] [[Chesa Boudin]] is successfully recalled and ousted from office, also on June 7. [[Mayor of San Francisco|Mayor]] [[London Breed]] will name Boudin's successor once the results are certified by the elections office and approved by the [[San Francisco Board of Supervisors|board of supervisors]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=June 7, 2022 Election Results - Summary {{!}} Department of Elections |url=https://sfelections.sfgov.org/june-7-2022-election-results-summary |access-date=2022-06-08 |website=sfelections.sfgov.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mai-Duc |first=Zusha Elinson and Christine |date=2022-06-07 |title=San Francisco District Attorney Chesa Boudin Recalled by Voters Amid Rising Murder Rate |language=en-US |work=The Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/san-francisco-district-attorney-chesa-boudin-faces-recall-election-11654603200 |access-date=2022-06-08 |issn=0099-9660}}</ref>

Republican candidate [[Brad Finstad]] defeats Democratic candidate [[Jeff Ettinger]] to serve the remainder of Hagedorn's term.<ref>{{cite web |last=Orenstein |first=Walker |date=August 10, 2022 |title=Finstad's win in Minnesota's 1st Congressional District explained |url=https://www.minnpost.com/elections/2022/08/finstads-win-in-minnesotas-1st-congressional-district-explained/ |access-date=2022-08-14 |website=MinnPost |language=en-US}}</ref>
* After the death of Representative [[Don Young]] (R, [[Alaska's at-large congressional district|Alaska at large]]), Alaska elects Democrat [[Mary Peltola]] in the [[2022 Alaska's at-large congressional district special election|special election]] held on August 16, famously defeating former governor [[Sarah Palin]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=Liz Ruskin, Alaska Public |date=2022-10-17 |title=Peltola trounces Palin and Begich in September fundraising, wins over Don Young loyalists |url=https://alaskapublic.org/2022/10/17/peltola-trounces-palin-and-begich-in-september-fundraising-wins-over-don-young-loyalists/ |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=Alaska Public Media |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Eric Bradner |date=August 31, 2022 |title=Sarah Palin loses special election for Alaska House seat |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/08/31/politics/alaska-house-seat-ranked-choice-ballots/index.html |access-date=2022-09-01 |website=CNN}}</ref>
* Two special elections were held in New York on August 23. [[2022 New York's 19th congressional district special election|The first]] is held in the 19th district to determine a successor for [[Antonio Delgado]] after he became [[Lieutenant Governor of New York|New York's lieutenant governor]]. The special election is narrowly won by Democratic candidate [[Pat Ryan (politician)|Pat Ryan]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Mahoney |first=Bill |date=August 24, 2022 |title=Democrat Pat Ryan wins bellwether special election in New York's Hudson Valley |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/08/24/pat-ryan-molinaro-new-york-special-00053458 |website=Politico |language=en-US}}</ref> [[2022 New York's 23rd congressional district special election|The second]] is held in the 23rd district, vacated after [[Tom Reed (politician)|Tom Reed]] resigned over accusations of sexual abuse and misconduct. Republican [[Joe Sempolinski]] wins the special election with 53.3 percent of the vote over Democrat Max Della Pia with 46.7 percent of the vote. The following is a list of events from the year 2022 in the United States.
Politically, the United States continued to be dominated by a culture war, with the issue of abortion gaining special attention amidst the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade with its ruling on Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, sparking protests across the country. America also saw labor unions gain increased traction, with Apple, Starbucks and Amazon among the most notable targets. In conjunction, increased attention to critical race theory, the instruction of gender identity in schools, and the ongoing investigations into both former president Donald Trump and the January 6th attack gained political attention. Mass shootings also became an increasingly common phenomenon, with 641 occurring in 2022 as of December 28, varying from those targeting schools (including the deadliest shooting of the year) to bias-motivated incidents which have targeted racial and sexual minorities.

In the economy, the United States remained heavily impacted by the global inflation surge, a simultaneous stock market decline and a heavy increase in gasoline prices, all partly due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. America's largest tech companies were hit especially hard by the economy, with Meta Platforms in particular losing nearly $700 billion in valuation. The Federal Reserve gained increased attention with a series of its first aggressive interest rate hikes in years, a trend which continued in 2023, with the federal funds rate by year's end reaching 4.4%. 2022 also marked a period of acquisitions within the tech industry as well, notably Elon Musk's acquisition of Twitter and Microsoft's ongoing buyout of Activision Blizzard. Later in the year, the US saw the first major challenges to its gratuity culture; tipflation, as it has since become known, has caused Americans to lower their tips.
